scope: Official protocol and temporal methodology reading plus deterministic synthetic local experiment; no chain RPC, live payloads, account provisioning, installs, spending, external sends or deployments.
citation_note: retrieval_refs identify observed tool retrievals; URLs and sections make source review independently inspectable. Source facts are paraphrases. Inferences are explicitly separated.

sources.title: MariaDB bitemporal tables
sections_reviewed: System-versioning and application-time combination; temporal periods
supported_facts: Bitemporal tables combine system-versioned history with application-time periods.
project_inferences: Separate domain time and knowledge history; product availability still needs separate evidence.

sources.title: MariaDB system-versioned tables
sections_reviewed: History introduction; historical AS OF queries; transaction-precise history caveat
supported_facts: System-versioned tables retain historical row states; AS OF selects a previous state.
project_inferences: An operational database update history alone does not verify historical public availability.

sources.title: Ethereum JSON-RPC
sections_reviewed: Block parameter tags (lines 325-343); eth_getFilterChanges removed/log provenance fields (lines 1805-1834); filter timeout
supported_facts: Block parameters distinguish latest, safe and finalized.
A removed log indicates removal due to a chain reorganization; logs include transaction/block provenance.
project_inferences: Retain original log evidence and dated reorg conclusions; no universal EVM finality inheritance.

sources.title: Ethereum proof of stake
sections_reviewed: Checkpoint finality and stake votes; economic consequences of finalized reversion; finality stall (lines 300-329)
supported_facts: Checkpoint finality depends on stake-voting rules.
Reverting finalized history has slashable-stake consequences; finality can stall.
project_inferences: Do not promise zero finality risk or a fixed universal completion delay.

sources.title: ERC-20 token standard
supported_facts: decimals is optional metadata.
Transfer event specifies from, to and raw value, including required zero-value event handling.
project_inferences: Transfer fields alone do not establish consideration, sale price or beneficial ownership; missing precision remains unknown.

sources.title: Solana RPC overview
supported_facts: Processed observations may roll back; confirmed and finalized are distinct commitment levels.
Public endpoints are shared, can return rate-limit or access-block responses, and are not intended as production capacity.
project_inferences: Persist explicit commitment and provider coverage; confirmed is not finalized and endpoint documentation is not entitlement proof.

sources.title: Solana create token account
sections_reviewed: Token account definition, owner fields and ATA/non-ATA distinction (lines 35-163)
supported_facts: Token accounts hold a mint balance with token-operation authority distinct from base account program ownership.
Custom token accounts exist beyond the associated-account convention.
project_inferences: Multiple accounts can share one direct authority; neither account nor authority count is a person count.

sources.title: Solana transfer tokens
supported_facts: Token transfers move token balances; TransferChecked checks expected mint precision.
Owner or authorized delegate permissions can authorize transfers.
project_inferences: A token transfer instruction alone does not establish an economic sale.

sources.title: Solana token model
sections_reviewed: Mint supply/precision and mint/freeze authority; token account fields (lines 60-119)
supported_facts: Mint and freeze authority have separate permission roles.
Token account authority is distinct from mint authority.
project_inferences: Permission role labels are not human or beneficial-owner labels.

sources.title: Solana terminology
supported_facts: Rooted history and finality relate to consensus and lockout.
PDA signing uses program authorization rather than an ordinary private key signature.
project_inferences: A queried authority can be a program-derived authority; raw authority does not identify an independent person.

sources.title: Solana getTokenLargestAccounts
sections_reviewed: Method result limit (line 17); commitment configuration; response context slot and balance fields
supported_facts: Method returns the 20 largest token accounts for a mint with response context.
project_inferences: A top-20 response is partial coverage, not a full mint owner universe.

sources.title: Solana getTokenAccountsByOwner
sections_reviewed: Owner/mint/program parameters; commitment/minContextSlot; response context and parsed owner fields (lines 17-55,157,200)
supported_facts: Method filters by owner and mint or program, and returns a context slot.
Outer account owner and parsed token-data owner have distinct roles.
project_inferences: Owner-filtered accounts do not establish beneficial-owner census; a minimum context bound does not select an exact historic state.

sources.title: Solana SetAuthority
sections_reviewed: Authority changes and separate roles; instruction/source reference (lines 35-53)
supported_facts: SetAuthority changes or revokes particular authority roles on mint/token accounts.
project_inferences: Current authority must not silently substitute for point-in-time historical authority.

sources.title: Official Solana Token Program documentation
supported_facts: Auxiliary accounts exist; multisig authorities can govern mint and token-account permission roles.
project_inferences: A single authority address can represent a signer set, without establishing economic beneficial owners.

sources.title: Official Token Program state.rs at pinned revision
sections_reviewed: Mint fields (retrieval lines 1191-1218); Account (1325-1366); AccountState (1512-1534); Multisig (1541-1559)
supported_facts: Mint, Account and Multisig encode different authority, balance, precision, state and signer fields.
project_inferences: Use protocol-field meanings explicitly; source inspection does not validate a live account or prove economic ownership.

limitations: No primary source was comprehensively audited except the short bitemporal page.
No chain payload, source availability archive, historical market sample, database migration or provider entitlement was verified.
Official method semantics do not guarantee provider retention, historic completeness, data rights or timely finality.
Pinned Token Program source was inspected but not compiled or executed.
MariaDB reading supplies conceptual temporal context; the project PostgreSQL architecture remains unchanged.
